concepts.title: Challenge of Building Democracy and the First General Election

questions.q: Using the method 'Challenge of Building Democracy and the First General Election', work with: independent_election_commission = 24, prepared_electoral_rolls = 60, universal_adult_franchise = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of free_and_fair_election.

Take the relation taught for 'Challenge of Building Democracy and the First General Election' and work with: independent_election_commission = 400, prepared_electoral_rolls = 24, universal_adult_franchise = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of free_and_fair_election.
Explain in your own words what 'Challenge of Building Democracy and the First General Election' refers to.
questions.a: Unlike many newly free nations that slipped into one-man or one-party rule, India chose competitive democracy from day one: an independent Election Commission under Sukumar Sen prepared constituency boundaries and voter lists, registered every adult citizen as a voter regardless of literacy, and ran a first nationwide poll that skeptics had called an impossible gamble.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Challenge of Building Democracy and the First General Election'.
questions.a: Democracy was treated as the method for solving public problems, not a luxury to be postponed until a country became rich or literate.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Challenge of Building Democracy and the First General Election', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Seat Share versus Vote Share under First-Past-The-Post

questions.q: Using the method 'Seat Share versus Vote Share under First-Past-The-Post', work with: seats_won = 30, total_seats = 3, vote_share = 0.45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of opposition_split.

Take the relation taught for 'Seat Share versus Vote Share under First-Past-The-Post' and work with: seats_won = 30, total_seats = 15, vote_share = 0.45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of opposition_split.
Explain in your own words what 'Seat Share versus Vote Share under First-Past-The-Post' refers to.
questions.a: Under the first-past-the-post system used in India, a party that wins more votes than any rival takes the entire seat of each constituency, so its share of seats inflates far beyond its share of votes; the Congress turned 45 per cent of votes in 1952 into 74 per cent of Lok Sabha seats, while the divided opposition stayed badly under-rewarded.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Seat Share versus Vote Share under First-Past-The-Post'.
questions.a: The winner-takes-all conversion of votes into seats artificially magnified Congress majorities because non-Congress votes split among many rivals.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Seat Share versus Vote Share under First-Past-The-Post', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Communist Victory in Kerala and Dismissal under Article 356

questions.q: Using the method 'Communist Victory in Kerala and Dismissal under Article 356', work with: communist_party_majority = 80, independent_support = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of kerala_government_of_1957.

Take the relation taught for 'Communist Victory in Kerala and Dismissal under Article 356' and work with: communist_party_majority = 12, independent_support = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of kerala_government_of_1957.
Explain in your own words what 'Communist Victory in Kerala and Dismissal under Article 356' refers to.
questions.a: In the March 1957 assembly elections the Communist Party won 60 of 126 seats and, with five independents, formed a ministry under E. M. S. Namboodiripad -- the first government anywhere to be brought to power by democratic communist election; in 1959 the Centre dismissed it under Article 356 after a Congress-backed liberation struggle, a step still cited as a misuse of emergency powers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Communist Victory in Kerala and Dismissal under Article 356'.
questions.a: Kerala 1957 proved both that communists could win office through ballots and that a Centre-state confrontation over a radical elected government could end in constitutional dismissal.

concepts.title: Congress as a Social and Ideological Coalition with Factional Tolerance

questions.q: Using the method 'Congress as a Social and Ideological Coalition with Factional Tolerance', work with: ideological_coalition = 300, social_coalition = 200, tolerated_factions = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of congress_system.

Take the relation taught for 'Congress as a Social and Ideological Coalition with Factional Tolerance' and work with: ideological_coalition = 3, social_coalition = 24, tolerated_factions = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of congress_system.
Explain in your own words what 'Congress as a Social and Ideological Coalition with Factional Tolerance' refers to.
questions.a: Congress dominance differed from one-party regimes elsewhere because it operated under free competition: the party was a rainbow coalition of classes, castes, religions and languages, an ideological spectrum from conservative to radical, and it tolerated internal factions so that rivalry stayed inside the party rather than producing breakaways -- the arrangement political scientists called the Congress system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Congress as a Social and Ideological Coalition with Factional Tolerance'.
questions.a: Because every group and ambition found room inside the ruling party, competition happened within the Congress, and opposition parties could only pressurise it from the margins.

concepts.title: Emergence of Opposition Parties in the 1950s

questions.q: Using the method 'Emergence of Opposition Parties in the 1950s', work with: bharatiya_jana_sangh = 4, communist_party = 20, socialist_party = 150, swatantra_party = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of opposition_parties.

Take the relation taught for 'Emergence of Opposition Parties in the 1950s' and work with: bharatiya_jana_sangh = 25, communist_party = 15, socialist_party = 360, swatantra_party = 60. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of opposition_parties.
Explain in your own words what 'Emergence of Opposition Parties in the 1950s' refers to.
questions.a: A range of parties contested the first decades of elections though they won only token seats: the Socialist Party born from the Congress Socialist group of 1934 and forced out by the 1948 ban on dual membership; the Communist Party with its disciplined cadre that split in 1964 into CPI and CPI(M); and the Bharatiya Jana Sangh of 1951 with its one country, one culture agenda -- together they kept democratic criticism alive under Congress dominance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Emergence of Opposition Parties in the 1950s'.
questions.a: Even token representation mattered: principled criticism checked the ruling party, kept alternatives alive, and groomed future national leaders.
